title: Generate Balanced Parentheses
statement: A template engine wants to enumerate every distinct way to nest n pairs of brackets. Given a non-negative integer n, return every string made of exactly n '(' characters and n ')' characters that is well-formed, meaning every prefix of the string contains at least as many '(' as ')'. Return the strings as a list sorted lexicographically; note that '(' sorts before ')', so for n = 2 the answer is ["(())", "()()"]. For n = 0, return a list containing only the empty string: [""]. Build the strings character by character and prune invalid branches as you go rather than generating all 2^(2n) strings and filtering.
hints: You are building a string one character at a time, and at each position you have at most two choices. What rule tells you a choice can never lead to a valid string, so you can skip that whole branch?

Track two counters as you recurse: open_used and close_used. You may add '(' while open_used < n, and you may add ')' only while close_used < open_used — comparing close_used to n instead lets invalid strings like ')(' through.

Recurse with a path list: if len(path) == 2n, join and record it; otherwise try '(' when open_used < n (append, recurse with open_used+1, pop), then try ')' when close_used < open_used (append, recurse with close_used+1, pop). Sort the collected results before returning.
